summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck major Russian logistics and energy infrastructure, destroying a Wildberries distribution hub in Voronezh region and igniting the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery in Orenburg region, 1,500–2,000 km from the border. Russia responded with ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Myrhorod, killing at least 10 civilians and wounding dozens. Ukraine's July 'middle strike' campaign degraded Russian air defenses, bridges, fuel terminals, and UAV control nodes across occupied territories.
key_points: Ukrainian drones destroyed the Wildberries logistics hub in Alexandrovka, Voronezh region, burning 16,000 and 75,000 sq m facilities worth 11 billion rubles. (Source: @eRadarrua/104894)
Ukrainian drones hit the Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery and a mechanical plant producing artillery shell casings in Orsk, Orenburg region, 1,500–2,000 km from Ukraine. (Source: @eRadarrua/104892)

Russia launched ballistic missiles at Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Myrhorod district, Poltava region, with a missile striking a children's hospital in Kyiv. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/70043, @mon1tor_ua/70054, @mon1tor_ua/70062)
Russian guided aerial bombs hit Sumy region, wounding 25 people; Dnipropetrovsk region attacks killed a 15-year-old boy and injured two children. (Source: @UkraineNow/83349, @eRadarrua/104895)

Ukraine's July 'middle strike' campaign destroyed 14 bridges in occupied territories, 9+ air defense/EW systems (S-400, Buk, Pantsir-S2, Murmansk-BN), 10+ UAV control points, and fuel terminals in Kerch, Shakhtarsk, and a Black Sea tanker. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)
Ukraine is fortifying the Chornobyl exclusion zone, 15 km from Belarus, with trenches, anti-FPV nets, and cleared fields of fire. (Source: @UkraineNow/83344)
Russia received a new batch of North Korean ballistic missiles and prepares to receive North Korean troops, per Zelensky. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32350)
Turkey plans to supply Ukraine with decommissioned U.S.-made MLRS launchers and ATACMS ballistic missiles. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32346)

points: Ukrainian drones destroyed the Wildberries logistics hub in Alexandrovka, Voronezh region, burning 16,000 and 75,000 sq m facilities worth 11 billion rubles, one of Russia's newest and largest distribution centers launched in November 2025. (Source: @eRadarrua/104894)

Ukrainian drones hit the Orsknefteorgsintez oil refinery and a mechanical plant producing artillery shell casings in Orsk, Orenburg region, at a distance of 1,500–2,000 km from the Ukrainian border. (Source: @eRadarrua/104892)

Ukraine's July 'middle strike' campaign destroyed 14 bridges and crossings in occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, and Crimea, complicating Russian troop and ammunition transfers. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)

Ukrainian strikes eliminated at least nine Russian air defense and EW systems including S-400, Buk, Pantsir-S2, and Murmansk-BN, plus over 10 UAV control points, hangars at Saki and Gvardeyskoye airfields, drone depots, and an FSB center in Kherson region. (Source: @UkraineNow/83343)

Ukraine is fortifying the Chornobyl exclusion zone, 15 km from Belarus, with trenches, defensive positions, checkpoints, anti-FPV metal nets, cleared tree lines, and widened roads for military vehicles. (Source: @UkraineNow/83344)

Turkey intends to supply Ukraine with decommissioned U.S.-made MLRS launchers and ATACMS ballistic missiles, signaling Ankara's willingness to lift previous restrictions on military aid. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32346)

sections.threat_assessment: Ukraine's demonstrated ability to strike strategic Russian logistics and energy infrastructure at 1,500–2,000 km range significantly expands the threat envelope for Russian rear areas. The systematic degradation of Russian air defenses (S-400, Buk, Pantsir-S2, Murmansk-BN) and bridge networks in occupied territories will compound Russian sustainment challenges. Russia's reliance on North Korean ballistic missiles and potential troop deployments indicates munitions shortages and manpower constraints. The introduction of Turkish-supplied ATACMS and MLRS could further extend Ukrainian strike reach. Russian ballistic missile attacks on Ukrainian cities, including a children's hospital, signal continued terror bombing campaigns. The fortification of the Chornobyl zone suggests Ukraine anticipates a potential northern axis threat from Belarus.
sections.regional_response: Turkey's decision to supply decommissioned U.S.-made MLRS and ATACMS to Ukraine, despite previous restrictions and Ukrainian strikes on Turkish vessels, marks a significant shift in Ankara's policy and may pressure other NATO members to accelerate long-range missile transfers. The U.S. Patriot production license refusal, driven by commercial concerns, highlights allied industrial constraints. Belarus remains a staging concern given the Chornobyl fortifications. North Korean missile and troop support to Russia deepens the Russia-Iran-North Korea axis, likely prompting enhanced South Korean and Japanese security coordination with Ukraine. Regional supply chain disruptions from Russian strikes on Ukrainian logistics hubs (Nova Poshta, San-Park) are driving 15–25% price increases in Kyiv.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Wildberries hub destruction (launched November 2025) and Orsk refinery strike demonstrate Ukrainian precision targeting of recently commissioned, high-value economic nodes. The 1,500–2,000 km strike range implies either new drone variants or forward operating bases. The abandonment of Huliaipole fortifications due to personnel shortages reveals critical Ukrainian manpower gaps despite 99% construction completion. Russian domestic cohesion claims (Belgorod unity) contrast with the scale of Ukrainian rear-area strikes. The Tu-95MS relocation to Engels suggests imminent cruise missile campaign preparation. Ukrainian TCC corruption investigations (76 officials, 2,500 illegal bookings, 6,500 canceled VLK decisions) indicate internal mobilization friction. Supply chain collapse from warehouse attacks forces direct-to-store delivery models.
